solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Intuitive version initially is clear, but misinterpreted

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of version

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something misinterpreted is read wrongly, so the gathered letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's instinctive take on a text was plain enough, yet people got it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misinterpreted' rearranges only the word clear, into CERAL; 'but' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A visceral reaction comes from gut feeling rather than reasoning, so it is instinctive.

clue.text: Refuse to allow tailless domesticated fowl

parts.note: to refuse to allow something is to ban it

indicators.note: tailless means the final letter of the word is docked

parts.note: a domesticated animal is tame

explanation.surface: A farmer will not permit a tame bird whose tail has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' cuts the last letter from TAME, leaving TAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of domestic chicken, a kind of fowl.

clue.text: I'm coming back into quiet home

indicators.note: into tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a quiet, submissive animal is docile

indicators.note: coming back means the letters of I'm are read in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone announces their return to a peaceful house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' gives MI, which goes 'into' the word for quiet, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A domicile is the formal or legal word for the place where a person lives.

clue.text: Skilful line not seen in Dutch crockery

indicators.note: not seen in means the line is missing from the pottery's name

parts.note: Delft is the blue-and-white pottery made in the Dutch town of Delft

explanation.surface: A deft craftsman's decoration doesn't appear on some Dutch plates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not seen in' removes L from DELFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft means neat and quick with the hands, a synonym for skilful.

clue.text: Crazy: equipment almost entirely for a song

parts.note: crazy means mad
a rig is a set of equipment, as in a drilling rig

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by one letter at its end

parts.note: entirely means all, as in all wrong

explanation.surface: It's madness to buy almost all your gear just for one song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' takes the last letter off ALL, leaving AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a Renaissance part-song for several unaccompanied voices.

clue.text: Lunar feature cold? Very much not hot

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: not here tells us the hot letter is left out of the word

parts.note: rather can mean very much, as in 'I rather like it'
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Is the moon's surface chilly? Certainly not warm, says the astronomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very much' as RATHER is the colloquial 'I rather like it'; 'not' drops the H for hot.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon's surface is pitted with craters, bowl-shaped hollows left by impacts.

clue.text: Story-teller in bar getting upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a rail is a bar, as in a towel rail

explanation.surface: A yarn-spinner in a pub becomes agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting upset' turns RAIL upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling stories is a euphemism for telling lies, so a story-teller can be a liar.

clue.text: Source of flavour in beer — the culminating touch

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A dash of flavouring added to the beer is the final flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing part of a show or piece, its climactic last element.

clue.text: With a passing fancy, each approach is to disappear with time

parts.note: a fad is a short-lived craze
ea is the abbreviation for each, as on price tags
a way is a method or approach

explanation.surface: Every attempt at following a craze is bound to fizzle out eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: To fade away is to dwindle gradually until gone, as memories or sounds do over time.

clue.text: Man from Edinburgh, say, to rush, avoiding a round

indicators.note: avoiding means the round letter is kept out of the word

parts.note: to scoot is to dash off quickly
O is round in shape, so it stands for a round

explanation.surface: An Edinburgh man hurries home rather than buy a round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Edinburgh is the capital of Scotland, so a man from there is an example of a Scot.

clue.text: Pleasant disposing of new cold dessert

indicators.note: disposing of means getting rid of the new letter from the word

parts.note: pleasant means nice

explanation.surface: A nice treat gets rid of the new chilled pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice is a frozen sweet such as ice cream or a water ice served after a meal.

clue.text: Studying front of car before driving

indicators.note: before puts the car's letter ahead of the next piece
the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: driving, as in driving a nail home, can mean ramming

explanation.surface: A learner revising for a test in the car before the driving exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Cramming is intensive last-minute studying for an exam.

clue.text: They don't appreciate popular Government's initial taxes

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable, as in 'the in crowd'

indicators.note: initial means only the opening letter of Government's is used

parts.note: rates are local taxes on property in Britain

explanation.surface: Voters ungrateful for a popular government's first taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrates are ungrateful people, those who show no thanks for what they receive.

clue.text: Uproar with rubbish around capital of Italy

indicators.note: around means the rubbish goes round the other letter

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Protest erupts over litter surrounding Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of' looks like it means Rome, but it just gives I, the first letter of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot is a violent public disturbance, a scene of uproar.

clue.text: Commemorative article I brought in about failing railway

indicators.note: brought in means the I is put inside the other letters
failing suggests breaking down, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A memorial piece I was given about a collapsing railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges the word about into OBTUA, and 'brought in' places I inside it to make OBITUA.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is a newspaper notice marking someone's death and recalling their life.

clue.text: Fielder in error

definitions.meaning: a cricket fielding position beside the wicketkeeper, and the player there

explanation.surface: A cricket player who has made a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a slip fields close behind the batsman; separately, a slip is a minor blunder.

clue.text: Post Office sure upset pretentious type

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A post office is certain to annoy a show-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseur is someone who puts on airs to impress, an affected person.

clue.text: Starry celebration given by commander-in-chief? About time

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration

indicators.note: about means the commander's letters go around the time letter

explanation.surface: A glittering party thrown by the top general, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' places T inside CIC to make CTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Galactic means relating to a galaxy, the vast system of stars.

clue.text: Shy about learner working in group

indicators.note: about means the shy word goes round the other letters

parts.note: coy means shy or bashful
L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
on means working, as a switched-on machine is

explanation.surface: A timid trainee employed among a team of colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony is a group, such as a community of settlers or a colony of ants.

clue.text: Boat's propeller observed initially beside a river

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of observed is taken

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A boat's engine part spotted at first next to a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar is a pole with a blade used to row, propelling a boat by hand.

clue.text: Ring up, getting venue for swimming

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a loop is a ring shape

explanation.surface: Phoning someone to arrange somewhere to swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring up' looks like a phone call, but 'Ring' is LOOP and 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool is a swimming pool, a place where people go to swim.

clue.text: Three players heading for tour, going to South American city

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a city in Brazil, often called simply Rio

explanation.surface: A band of three, starting a tour, heading to Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three musicians playing together.

clue.text: Deafening, behold, and extremely unbalanced

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, first and last, of unbalanced are taken

explanation.surface: Look at that racket: thoroughly off-kilter.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud means making a great deal of noise, enough to deafen.

clue.text: European celebrity finding direction indicator?

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland, a European
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A famous person from Europe is set to show us the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is figurative: the pole star is an example of something that shows direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The pole star, Polaris, sits almost directly above the North Pole and so shows navigators where north is.

clue.text: Fail to appreciate development of region

indicators.note: development suggests the letters evolving into a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Planners overlook how an area is being built up.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to take no notice of it, failing to recognise its worth.

clue.text: I will avoid various coal-fires out of doors

indicators.note: will avoid tells us one letter is left out of the jumble
various suggests many different arrangements, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone vows to steer clear of assorted coal-burning hearths and stay outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges the letters of COAL-FIRES, and 'I will avoid' tells you to drop the I first.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco is borrowed from Italian and means in the open air, as with outdoor dining.
